_readme: Dutch VAT rules for LEDGR (CMP-014, CMP-013, FR-VAT-001, FR-AR-002).
This file is DATA. scripts/load_vat_rules.py loads it into vat_treatment /
vat_rate / vat_rubriek / vat_treatment_rubriek, and a rate change is another
file loaded the same way - no migration, no deploy, no code change. See
docs/decisions/ADR-027-effective-dated-tax-rules.md.
EVERY RULE ROW CARRIES valid_from AND NOTHING ELSE.
The rule in force on a date is the row with the greatest valid_from on or
before it. There is deliberately no valid_to: an end date would have to be
written onto an existing row when the next rule arrives, and a reference
table you have to go back and edit is one where history can be rewritten by
accident. Superseding is an insert.
A CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING: inserting a row with a valid_from in the past
silently changes what applied then. That is what CMP-014 forbids near a
filed period, and the database refuses it - see vat_rule_not_behind_a_filing()
in migration 0028.
PROVENANCE - READ THIS BEFORE A RETURN IS FILED.
source is 'provisional-subset'. The RATES are the well-known ones and the
rubriek codes are the official 1a-5b set. What is NOT verified against the
Belastingdienst's own publication is the treatment-to-rubriek MAPPING: which
rubriek a given treatment's turnover and VAT belong in is the substance of
FR-VAT-001, which is not built. Getting a mapping wrong misstates a return
without misstating the ledger, so it is exactly the kind of error that
survives every other check in this system.
CMP-014 is about the machinery - effective dating, and history that cannot
be rewritten under a filed period. That machinery is complete and tested.
The dataset it carries is a starting point.
source_note: Rates are the published Dutch ones; the rubriek mapping is provisional and belongs to FR-VAT-001.
_treatments_note: FR-AR-002's eight treatments. `code` is what ledger_account.default_vat_code
holds and what 0024 constrains, so the strings are fixed by what already
Two of them - btw_21 and btw_9 - name a RATE in an identifier that has to
outlive it. btw_9 was 6% until 2019 and btw_21 was 19% until 2012, so the
code already lies about part of its own history. `role` is the stable
semantics and is what any rule should be written against; the code is an
identifier and nothing more. ADR-027 records the rename as owed work.
_rates_note: rate is a percentage as a decimal STRING - 21.00, not 0.21 and never a JSON
number. NFR-031 prohibits floating point anywhere in the calculation path,
and a rate is the first multiplier in it: json.dumps of a Python float
produces a number here and the loader rejects it, exactly as
ledger.post_entry rejects a JSON number for an amount.

The 2001-01-01 rows are a floor, not a claim that the rate began then. They
exist so every date this system can hold resolves to something rather than
to NULL - a lookup that returns nothing is far more dangerous than one that
returns a rate somebody has to check.

_mapping_note: Which box a treatment's turnover and its VAT land in. PROVISIONAL - this is
the part FR-VAT-001 owns and the part most likely to be wrong.
vat_rubriek is null where the treatment produces no output VAT for the
seller, which is not the same as producing zero: a reverse-charged supply
has no VAT to report in a 1x box at all, whereas a 0% supply has an amount
that happens to be zero. Collapsing the two would put figures in boxes the
Belastingdienst does not expect them in.
